newsitem.title: USA: Glickman hopes to unveil CRP rules by Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: Glickman hopes to unveil CRP rules by Wednesday.

text.p: Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman said Monday he hoped to unveil the new set of rules for the Conservation Reserve Program before departing on a visit to South Africa on Wednesday.

"The rule will be announced hopefully this week. Hopefully it will be before I leave. I'm leaving Wednesday afternoon," he told reporters at a briefing on his trip to attend the U.S.-South Africa Binational Commission meetings.

USDA Acting Deputy Under Secretary, Farm and Foreign Agricultural Services Dallas Smith told reporters the intent was to start signup up as soon as the final rule was published in the Federal Register.
"It will be effective immediately and then we can start planning the actual opening day from there," he said.

Asked about talk on Capitol Hill of legislation to extend existing contracts, Glickman said: "I think that will have trouble clearing through the legislative process all the way through...My personal belief is I hope there is no extension of the thing."
Glickman noted the pool of lands to be considered was not materially larger than what was initially proposed.

"The proof in the pudding in this is how we implement the program not the nature of lands that goes in in the beginning," Glickman said. "The role is to protect the most sensitive, most highly erodible lands in the country."
